title: Optimize Console: recommendation playback, preview diffs & immutable apply audit
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Optimize want non-disruptive cost recommendations (batching/caching/quantization) with a clear preview of runtime/cost/quality trade-offs and an auditable, immutable history of config applies and rollbacks. Current console UX surfaces recommendations as isolated cards but lacks a deterministic preview of how an apply will change runtime behavior and no single-playback surface to replay past applies for audit or debugging.

Goal: Ship a console workflow that lets operators: 1) preview the exact diff (config JSON + calculated cost/latency delta + sample inference traces) before applying; 2) run a sandboxed "playback"/rehearsal that simulates the apply against a mirrored traffic window; 3) create an immutable audit entry for every apply/rollback with links to the diff, who approved it, and automated regression signals. The UX should make safe rollbacks one-click and provide deterministic reason codes for why an apply was accepted or rejected by the platform.

Constraints: Must work for Hosted and Dedicated modes, respect RBAC (only approvers may execute), avoid expensive live replays for very large customers (provide sampled/simulated mode), and integrate with existing rollout APIs and telemetry.

Out of scope: Full on-prem packaging of the playback runner (will be tracked in a follow-up Private deployment story).
acceptance_criteria:
- Console shows a draft diff view for each recommendation with three panes: Config diff (JSON + human summary), Cost/Latency delta (per-token and per-request), and Sample inference traces highlighting potential quality changes.
- 'Playback' button triggers a simulated or sampled rehearsal run; results surface sample traces, expected cost delta, and failure/error rates in the UI within 5 minutes for typical accounts.
- Apply flow requires explicit approval from an approver role and creates an immutable audit record with: timestamp, actor, diff snapshot, playback results, canary policy applied, and a one-click rollback action.
- Rollback restores previous effective config and records a rollback audit entry; telemetry shows 0.99 probability of restored token-cost parity within 1 hour for Dedicated customers.
- UI integrates with rollout-API (ENG-4231) and audit-logging pipeline (ENG-5022).
- End-to-end e2e tests and a smoke test run in CI that asserts diff preview render, apply path, and rollback link presence.

qa_steps: Deploy feature branch to staging and enable Optimize:playback flag for test org 'opt-playback-01'
Create recommendations for batching and KV cache from sample workload using test dataset 'opt-demo-1'
Open recommendation card, verify diff preview shows JSON diff, human summary, and cost/latency delta
Run 'Simulate/Playback' - validate that simulated traces appear and metrics match expected sample outputs
Approve and Apply the recommendation as a user with 'Optimize Approver' role - verify audit entry is created and visible in Apply History tab
Trigger rollback from audit entry and confirm previous config is restored and a rollback audit entry exists
Run CI smoke tests to confirm e2e apply + rollback flow succeeds within timeout thresholds
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated by org; enable for 3 internal beta customers. 2) Monitor for false positives in simulated regressions and gather feedback. 3) Gradual ramp to all orgs over 2 weeks with ability to disable simulate mode via admin toggle. 4) Post-launch: iterate on quantization recs and non-sampled live rehearsal for Dedicated customers.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: full live replay is the most accurate but too expensive; decided on sampled and simulate modes with clear labeling. Immutable audit stores snapshots (immutable blob storage) to ensure future forensic reproducibility. UX decision: show 'confidence' score computed from offline eval set to help users weigh quality risk.
